issues.body: The prior-round finding is still present. Stage 2 says private values are shared t-of-n with t=floor((n-1)/2), and the F_share row again says it distributes a t-of-n sharing, while the record uses t as the maximum corrupt coalition and polynomial degree (including n=2t+1 and degree-2t products). For degree-t Shamir sharing, any t shares reveal no information, but reconstruction requires t+1 valid shares. The current wording conflates privacy/corruption threshold with reconstruction threshold in the pipeline and its ideal functionality.
issues.fix_hint: Replace both t-of-n descriptions with unambiguous degree-t Shamir terminology and explicitly state that any t shares reveal no information while t+1 valid shares reconstruct, with t=floor((n-1)/2). Check nearby threshold-open/reconstruction wording for the same convention.
issues.title: Shamir reconstruction threshold remains misstated as t-of-n

verdict.summary: Round 5 is stagnant: the round-4 threshold error remains unchanged in both the stage-2 description and the F_share ideal-functionality row. The document defines t=floor((n-1)/2) as the corruption/privacy threshold and later correctly describes degree-t sharing, where any t shares reveal no information. Calling that a t-of-n sharing is therefore inconsistent: degree-t Shamir reconstruction requires t+1 shares. Because this terminology occurs in the load-bearing pipeline and ideal-functionality descriptions of a security posture record, the document is not yet correct as scoped.
